The anatomical RIGHT leg is the FAR leg reaching toward lower-left, and its front shoe is the SUPPORT FOOT. Keep that shoe planted at its current sole contact position and facing southwest; do not just rotate the shoe. Redraw the connected right hip, knee and ankle into genuine landing compression: the right knee bends substantially, the shin leans forward over the ankle, and the pelvis and belly sink DOWN and slightly FORWARD toward the planted shoe. The pelvis-to-support-sole distance becomes visibly shorter by articulation. The chest/head follows the lowered pelvis while retaining its exact physical size. The near anatomical LEFT leg stays folded behind and OFF the ground; there are only two legs.
The result must read as the boy's weight being caught by his right leg, not a split-legged airborne pose with a flat shoe. Knee, ankle and shoe point along the same southwest travel axis, without outward roll. Preserve the rendering and props. No zoom, no whole-cutout translation, no new ground/shadow/effects. Single full transparent RGBA sprite, native at least 1024 square.
